fields.value: Strongest feature: Price answers the manuscript challenge with concrete internal evidence, identifying changed function, apostolic credentials, the grouping of Peter, James, the Twelve, and all apostles, and apparent redundancy as signs of editorial compromise. Principal limitation: These features do not uniquely indicate insertion, because Paul’s announced gospel gives verses 3 through 11 a plausible role in the resurrection argument, while an expanded list can unite witnesses without preserving competing factions. Live burden: Price must show that removing the passage improves the chapter and that editorial compromise explains the grouped credentials better than continuous composition despite no surviving manuscript without these verses. Locked score: The score of 80 reflects a specific, responsive, clearly articulated internal case with genuine evidential force, bounded by a strong contextual alternative and no external textual corroboration.

Strongest feature: White converts the dispute into a transmission-history test by asking why a text without verses 3 through 11 survives in none of the interconnected manuscript streams, directly confronting a consequence of Price’s reconstruction. Principal limitation: This absence is powerful negative evidence but not conclusive, because an insertion before every recoverable branch separated could leave surviving streams with the passage even if an earlier form existed. Live burden: White must establish that relevant branching predates the proposed insertion, or show why some pre-insertion lineage should have survived, without treating unanimous witnesses as certainty. Locked score: The score of 88 recognizes an exceptionally direct, coherent, well-supported challenge that sharply raises Price’s burden, while stopping short of a higher rating because the chronology needed to exclude universal early adoption remains unproved.
